Lessons.Title: Conic Sections in Polar Coordinates
ExplanationParagraphs: Focus-origin polar conic r=l/(1±e cosθ) or r=l/(1±e sinθ) depends on eccentricity e.
0≤e<1 describes ellipse (circle if e=0), e=1 parabola, e>1 hyperbola.
Convert x=r cosθ,y=r sinθ,r²=x²+y² and retain sign/domain restrictions after squaring.
Polar graph asymptotes occur where denominator vanishes; negative radius can reverse direction.
Describe focus, vertices and directrices from geometric parameter e and l.
Independent Cool-down: identify the standard conic, state relevant foci/axis features, and verify the equation with an independent point.
